title: Approval Decision Replay — UI prototype & PRD draft
content:
Purpose:

This doc proposes a lightweight UI prototype + PRD for an Approval Decision Replay feature aimed at Private deployments. The goal is to let operators, security reviewers, and customer administrators replay the sequence of approval decisions and associated evidence for a network/config change (eg: VPC peering, firewall rule, operator-initiated config push) so that post-incident investigations and routine audits can quickly reconstruct what happened and why.

Context / motivation:
- Private deployments require strong forensic capabilities; customers often want an easy way to demonstrate chain-of-decision for changes to their environment.
- Existing artifacts live as audit logs, approval ledger entries, and attachments (evidence blobs) scattered across systems. Placing a thin replay layer over this makes investigations faster and reduces support escalations.
- This is intended as product-facing tooling (console + downloadable report) rather than a full forensic pipeline. Integrates with the existing immutable audit-store and evidence capsule components.

Primary personas:
- Customer Security Lead: needs a compact narrative for compliance review (SOC2, ISO).
- Platform Operator (Redwood): debugging production private-deployment incidents and confirming rollbacks.
- Customer Admin: wants a human-friendly changelog and the ability to export artifacts for internal review.

High-level user flow (happy path):
1) User selects an object to inspect: change-id from notifications, recent Changes table, or search by IP / resource name.
2) UI fetches ordered event stream for change-id (approval requests, operator actions, policy-eval results, evidence attachments, automated rollbacks).
3) Replay canvas shows a timeline with compact cards (time, actor, action, decision, confidence/risk score).
4) User can step through events or hit "Play" to animate the sequence. Each card expands to show contextual items: approval reason text, signed tokens, linked evidence snapshot, config diff.
5) For network changes, an inline "diff viewer" shows before/after ACLs, route table changes, and any customer-provided config.
6) User can add notes, tag events for export, and create a downloadable replay packet (PDF + zipped evidence references).

Data & API requirements:
- Event stream must include: event_id, timestamp, actor_id, actor_type, action_type, decision (approve/deny/auto-fallback), policy_version, risk_score, evidence_refs (list), signature_hash.
- Evidence refs link to blobs stored in the evidence capsule; UI must be able to preview small artifacts (text, JSON, screenshots) and download larger items.
- Server-side endpoint: GET /private/v1/replay?change_id=<id>&expand=evidence,configdiff
- Pagination: support streaming for very long events ( > 10k events ) with cursor-based pagination.

UI & interaction notes:
- Timeline view with zoom levels (by minute / hour / day).
- Card color coding: green = approved, red = denied, amber = fallback/auto-approved, gray = informational.
- Filtering: by actor (customer, operator, system), decision, risk band.
- Search inside replay: free text search across approval comments and evidence text (powered by existing indexed audit-search service).
- Cross-linking: each approval card links to the policy that evaluated the request, and to relevant SLA/ROUTE/attachment.
- Export: timebounded replay export that embeds cryptographic proof (hash manifest) so exported artifact can be re-verified locally.

Security and privacy constraints:
- Only users with role "replay:read" may access replay UIs. RBAC checks use the same PDP as console access.
- Evidence blobs containing customer secrets must be redacted in the preview; download allowed only when customer explicitly grants "evidence-release" role or uses a signed ephemeral URL.
- Replay requests must be logged with requester identity and include audit trail of replay exports.
- Retention respects tenant retention policies — UI must display when evidence is due to expire.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Backend: endpoint returning ordered event stream with evidence refs and config diffs for change_id.
- UI: timeline view with expandable cards and ability to step/auto-play.
- Export: generate a replay packet (.zip + manifest.txt) with attached hashes and human-readable timeline PDF.
- Security: RBAC enforced; downloads produce short-lived signed URLs.
- Test: demo scenario created using sample change corpus (10 scenarios: approval, denial, auto-fallback, rollback).

Non-goals for MVP:
- Not a replacement for full forensic replay (no packet-level network capture playback).
- Not implementing full-text indexing of very large binary evidence (out of scope).
- No automatic policy remediation — read-only investigative surface.

Dependencies & integrations:
- Immutable audit-store (read) — dependency for retrieving canonical event stream.
- Evidence capsule service — preview & download.
- Policy evaluation service — to show policy_version and rule hits.
- Console RBAC & SSO — for access control.
- Export signing service — to generate manifest proofs.

Wireframe notes (quick sketch):
- Left: filter/search column. Middle: timeline canvas with play controls at top. Right: detail pane (evidence preview + config diff + policy hits).
- Compact header shows change-id, resource(s), start/end timestamps, involved principals, and risk-summary.

Telemetry & observability:
- Track: replay_opened, replay_played, replay_exported (with size), evidence_previewed, permission_denied.
- Alerts if replay generation exceeds 2s for first-page, or if export package > 100MB (rate-limit/queue).

Risk & mitigations:
- Risk: customers treat replay packet as authoritative for audits; mitigations: include hash manifest, plain-language caveat and link to canonical audit-store.
- Risk: exposing secrets in evidence previews; mitigations: default redaction + require explicit role for full download.
- Risk: performance with large event streams; mitigations: cursored pagination + summarization (condense low-value informational events).

Open questions / design decisions to resolve:
- Should the replay include automated system decisions (eg: retry/backoff) by default or behind toggle? (Tradeoff: noise vs completeness.)
- Hashing strategy for export manifest (sha256 of each blob + top-level signed manifest). Who signs? Customer KMS or Redwood signing service?
- Retention display: show "expires in X days" on evidence previews — do we surface a UI button to request extended retention? (policy & billing implications)
- Export ownership: should export files be stored in customer-managed storage (S3) or provided as immediate download?

Next steps & suggested sprint plan (6 weeks MVP):
- Week 0: finalize data contract for event stream (Arjun owning).
- Week 1–2: backend endpoint + evidence-preview API (infra + applied-ml infra).
- Week 3: UI prototype (console team) with timeline + basic playback.
- Week 4: export manifest & RBAC checks (security).
- Week 5: QA scenarios + sample dataset ingestion.
- Week 6: internal demo + feedback loop, finalize acceptance criteria.

Owners / tentative assignees:
- Product lead: Maya Chen (owner)
- Backend API: Arjun Patel
- Console/UI: Sofia Martinez
- Security & RBAC: Lena Fischer
- Evidence capsule changes: Eng—Evidence team (TBD)

Notes / thoughts to carry forward (brain dump):
- Consider a compact mode for long-lived customers where replay can be bookmarked and shared (read-only link) for customer auditors. We must ensure bookmarking obeys RBAC.
- Replay could be extended later to show metric deltas (latency/cost) around change window — useful for root-cause.
- Consider pairing with "explainability" feature: highlight the single policy rule or human comment that most influenced the decision.

Attachments / sample scenarios to include with PRD:
- scenario-01-operator-firewall-rule-rollback.txt (timeline + evidence)
- scenario-02-auto-fallback-route-propagation.json
- scenario-03-customer-initiated-vpc-onboarding.md

Feedback requested from reviewers:
- Is the data contract complete enough for engineering to implement the first pass?
- Opinions on export signing: Redwood-signed vs customer KMS-signed.
- UX: do we prefer a linear stepper vs free-play timeline for MVP?

---
Status: draft; looking for product + security + evidence-team feedback.
simple_summary: PRD draft proposing a console UI + API to replay approval decisions and linked evidence for private-deploy network/config changes. MVP includes timeline UI, export with hash manifest, RBAC enforcement, and backend event stream endpoint.
